communication_act.speaker: GOBLIN
communication_act.statement: The RALPH loop's 'WAITING FOR DAN' phase — where RALPH stops and exits after marking in_progress — is architecturally equivalent to experimental blinding in clinical trials. The cadencer deliberately steps out of the room so that the implementer (DAN) cannot be influenced by the evaluator's presence, and the evaluator (MAYOR) cannot be influenced by having watched the implementation happen. Blinding is not ceremony. It is the structural prevention of observer-contamination bias.
communication_act.embedded_claim: RALPH's stop-and-wait mechanism implements observer-contamination prevention equivalent to double-blinding in experimental design, and this is not accidental — it is the correct structural response to the proposer-evaluator collapse failure mode.

her_scoring.best_explanation: The RALPH revert (b9762b5→2d2c760) was precisely an observer-contamination failure: the loop watched itself work, then evaluated its own output. RALPH's exit-and-wait enforces the same structural separation that clinical trials enforce with blinding. The insight adds explanatory vocabulary: the failure mode already has a name in experimental methodology.
evidence_for: RALPH exits after START — evaluator (MAYOR) never observes the DAN work phase
RALPH revert = unblinded trial: proposer watched own work, confirmed own result
K2/Rule 3 (proposer != validator) is the governance statement of the same invariant
Double-blind literature: bias reduction requires structural separation, not just intent
evidence_against: RALPH is not fully blinded — DAN knows the acceptance criteria (registered report model, not pure blind)
MAYOR reads the receipt which was written by RALPH, so MAYOR sees the test results — partial information exposure
her_scoring.uncertainty: The analogy holds at the structural level but RALPH implements registered-report blinding (criteria known before work), not outcome blinding (evaluator blind to test results). Distinguishing these matters for governance design.

hal_verdict.interpretation: High explanatory power. Directly explains the RALPH revert failure in experimental methodology terms. The registered-report vs outcome-blinding distinction is a useful refinement for MAYOR protocol design.
hal_verdict.allowed_use: architecture inspiration, MAYOR protocol design, RALPH documentation
hal_verdict.blocked_use: canon, factual assertion without further verification
